reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Late August has a particular quality to it. Summer isn't over, but it's tilting. The light gets longer in the evenings, mornings feel a little sharper. It's the kind of week where nothing announces itself — no holiday, no milestone, just a Tuesday. And that's exactly the terrain where sobriety gets built or lost.

When I was drinking, ordinary Tuesdays were the enemy. There was nothing to celebrate, nothing to escape, just the low hum of a life I wasn't participating in. So I'd manufacture a reason. A drink to take the edge off a day that didn't actually have an edge. Now I understand that the unremarkable days are the whole game. Anyone can white-knuckle a wedding or a funeral. What changes your life is showing up, awake, for a Tuesday in August when nothing is happening.

Durant was paraphrasing Aristotle, and both of them were pointing at the same thing: you are not your intentions. You are the small things you actually do, over and over, when no one is watching and there's no reward waiting. Making the coffee. Taking the call. Going for the walk instead of the other thing. Sobriety isn't a decision you make once — it's a Tuesday you keep choosing. And a life gets built out of enough of them stacked end to end.
reflection.meditation: Sit for two minutes and think about what you'll actually do today. Not the big plan — the next real thing. Then go do it.

affirmations: I am building a life out of ordinary days, not dramatic ones.
Today I get to be present for whatever actually happens.
I am someone who follows through on the small things.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a Tuesday I can remember. Grateful for coffee that tastes like coffee, for a morning I didn't have to apologize my way into, for the quiet privilege of a day with no crisis in it. There was a version of me who couldn't imagine being okay with a day like this — and here I am, okay with it.
gratitude.closing: One more ordinary day. That's the whole gift.
